title: Dedicated pool per-tenant burst reconciliation and negative-balance policy
creator: Evan Park
description:
Scope and goal:
We need deterministic, auditable accounting for per-tenant consumption against Dedicated GPU pools that supports burst credits, negative-balance handling, and retroactive SLA credits. This ticket designs and implements:
  - a reconciliation pipeline that decomposes pool-level token consumption into per-tenant billed units (reserved throughput + burst) with sub-minute alignment to billing windows
  - a negative-balance policy for tenants who overspend burst capacity between invoice cycles, including automatic repayment using subsequent reserved throughput and safety cutoffs
  - retroactive SLA credit adjustments when we detect capacity degradation, with clear audit trail and invariant preservation for total pool accounting
Background / motivation:
We observed two customer issues in the last quarter: unexplained invoice variance for Dedicated customers and a post-mortem (INC-2025-021) showing a 27% mismatch between reported reserved throughput consumption and pool-level telemetry during a rolling kernel regression. Root causes were: (1) differing aggregation windows between serving runtime and billing, (2) burst assignment that treated pool-level burst as ephemeral and not durable in invoicing, and (3) no safe handling for tenants that temporarily exceeded reserved throughput resulting in negative meter states and manual credits.
Constraints and non-goals:
  - This ticket does not rework pricing model or UI invoicing templates; it focuses on internal accounting correctness and APIs used by billing engine
  - We will not change tenant quotas or runtime throttling behavior in this patch — only billing reconciliation and policy layers
Design overview:
  1) Aligned metering windows: introduce a canonical billing window (bucket key = pool_id + aligned_minute_timestamp) used by serving runtime to emit delta-meter events and by offline reconciler to aggregate. All downstream systems must use this canonical key.
  2) Burst decomposition: when pool-level delta exceeds sum(reserved_capacity_used), mark the remainder as pool-burst and run a deterministic per-tenant attribution algorithm: round-robin weighted by recent allocation share (last 5m), with ties broken by tenant_id hash. This creates per-tenant burst credits consumed.
  3) Negative balance model: tenants may have a transient negative burst balance. Policy: allow negative up to a configurable cap (default = 10% of reserved monthly commit) for up to N billing windows (default N=6), after which invoice-time enforcement triggers invoice-time debit or throttle flagging. Negative balances are settled first against future reserved throughput usage, then applied as invoice line items.
  4) SLA crediting: when reconciler detects pool degradation (compare expected tokens/second vs observed across kernels), compute retroactive SLA credits pro rata across active tenants based on their effective reserved consumption during the incident window. Credits are stored as immutable ledger entries with reference IDs for traceability.
Instrumentation and schema changes:
  - New event schema: BillingDeltaV2 { pool_id, aligned_minute_ts, tenant_id, reserved_tokens, burst_tokens, source_trace_id }
  - Add ledger table: dedicated_ledger_entries(partition_key=pool_id, entry_id, tenant_id, type=[charge|credit|settlement], amount_tokens, reason_code, created_by, created_at, irrevocable=true)
  - Add reconciler job: dedicated_reconciler_v2 (runs every minute, windowed by aligned_minute_ts).
APIs and outputs:
  - /billing/v1/pools/{pool_id}/reconciliations -> returns reconciliation batch ids and per-tenant delta summaries (read-only; used by billing-runner)
  - Export format for accounting: CSV/Parquet with canonical fields (pool_id, minute_ts, tenant_id, reserved, burst, ledger_ref)
  - Dashboard: billing/dedicated/reconciliations (new tab) with mismatch rate, negative_balance_exposure, recent SLA credits
Migration and rollout plan:
  - Phase 1 (canary): deploy reconciler in read-only mode to generate diffs between new per-tenant attribution and existing invoices (2 weeks). Surface diffs to internal billing QA dashboard.
  - Phase 2 (soft settle): enable ledger writes for non-production pools and customer sandboxes; run two parallel settlement runs for 1 invoice cycle and compare results programmatically.
  - Phase 3 (enforce): enable writes for production pools, enable negative-balance policy enforcement, and gate enforcement behind feature-flag with auto rollback.
Testing and validation:
  - Property tests that assert pool-level token conservation: sum(per-tenant_reserved + per-tenant_burst) == pool_delta for every aligned_minute_ts
  - Fuzz tests to exercise heavy burst scenarios with many tenants and ensure deterministic attribution
  - Long-run integration harness replays INC-2025-021 traffic into reconciler to validate SLA credit amounts match manual post-mortem calculations
Acceptance criteria:
  - Reconciler runs without producing >0.5% unresolved mismatch across pools for 7 consecutive days in canary
  - Negative-balance exposures are capped and observable (dashboard metric) and settled by automated settlement run
  - Billing-runner can consume reconciliation batches and produce identical invoice line-items to reference run for at least 2 customers in pilot
Key decisions and trade-offs considered:
  - Deterministic weighted round-robin attribution simplifies auditing at cost of potential short-term fairness anomalies; alternative was per-request attribution which is more precise but requires large changes to runtime tracing and higher cardinality events
  - Allowing bounded negative balances reduces operational friction for customers but adds complexity to settlements; chosen cap and window are conservative defaults that can be tuned per-contract
Links / artifacts:
  - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Dedicated+Metering+V2
  - Reconciler PR (in-flight): https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/423
  - Billing QA dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/billing/dedicated-reconciliations
  - Incident: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2025-021
Risks / rollbacks:
  - Risk: reconciliation introduces transient invoice deltas during phase changes. Mitigation: read-only canary and dry-run verifications before ledger writes.
  - Risk: performance impact on reconciler. Mitigation: parallelization by pool and minute window, shape tests on large pools.
Open questions:
  - Should negative-balance caps differ for auto-renew vs enterprise committed pools? (PM input required)
  - Should we provide per-tenant opt-out for negative-balance borrowing and prefer immediate throttling? (legal/accounting implications)
